workflows.name: devox-adversarial-dev
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants to build a complete application from scratch using adversarial development.
Triggers: "adversarial dev", "adversarial development", "build with adversarial", "gan dev",
          "adversarial build", "build app adversarially", "adversarial coding".
Does: Three-role GAN-inspired development — Planner creates spec with sprints, then a state-machine
      loop alternates between Generator (builds code) and Evaluator (attacks it) with hard pass/fail
      thresholds. The evaluator's job is to BREAK what the generator builds. If any criterion scores
      below 7/10, the sprint goes back to the generator with adversarial feedback. Stops on sprint
      failure after max retries.
NOT for: Bug fixes, PR reviews, refactoring existing code, simple one-off tasks.

Based on Anthropic's harness design article for long-running application development.
Separates planning, building, and evaluation into distinct roles with adversarial tension.

workflows.name: devox-architect
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants an architectural sweep, complexity reduction, or codebase health improvement.
Triggers: "improve architecture", "simplify codebase", "reduce complexity", "architectural sweep",
          "clean up architecture", "codebase health", "fix architecture".
Does: Scans codebase metrics -> analyzes architecture with principled lens -> plans targeted
      simplifications -> executes fixes with self-review loops (hooks) -> validates -> creates PR.
NOT for: Single-file fixes, feature development, bug fixes, PR reviews.

DAG workflow showcasing per-node hooks:
- PostToolUse hooks create organic quality loops (lint after write, self-review)
- PreToolUse hooks inject architectural principles before changes
- Different nodes have different trust levels and steering

workflows.name: devox-assist
workflows.description:
Use when: No other workflow matches the request.
Handles: Questions, debugging, exploration, one-off tasks, explanations, CI failures, general help.
Capability: Full Claude Code agent with all tools available.

workflows.name: devox-build-ready-plan
workflows.description:
Use when: You have a validated, designed idea/feature (Mission Intent + HLD diagrams approved)
          and need detailed build-ready specs across all planning domains.
Triggers: "build ready plan", "detailed specs", "feature planning", "sprint-ready plan",
          "enterprise plan", "l3 planning", "build specs",
          "create feature plan", "create specs", "write the plan".
Does:
  Reads Mission Intent / Enhancement Brief, Enterprise Context, and HLD diagrams from
  artifacts (sub-workflow mode) or $ARGUMENTS (standalone mode), then runs 6 parallel
  planning personas (PO, BA, UX, Architect, Governance, Features List), resolves
  cross-domain conflicts, and assembles a final build-ready plan + executive summary.
  Saves per-persona markdown sections to disk before the assembler runs, keeping AI
  context windows small and reproducible.
Outputs (saved to $ARTIFACTS_DIR):
  build-ready-plan/po-scope.md           — Product scope, user stories, MoSCoW
  build-ready-plan/ba-requirements.md    — Functional requirements + acceptance criteria
  build-ready-plan/ux-specification.md   — Journey maps, component inventory, design gaps
  build-ready-plan/solution-architecture.md — Architecture spec + ADRs
  build-ready-plan/governance-requirements.md — Compliance implementation checklist
  build-ready-plan/features-list.md      — Enterprise-constrained feature table
  build-ready-plan/build-plan.md         — Consolidated build-ready feature plan
  build-ready-plan/executive-summary.md  — Stakeholder one-page summary
Works as:
  Standalone: run after concept-validation, devox-enterprise-context-validator, and devox-generate-design-overview.
  Sub-workflow: called by product-idea-to-enterprise-plan after all gates are approved.
NOT for: Idea validation (use concept-validation), design diagrams (use devox-generate-design-overview),
         enterprise rules resolution (use devox-enterprise-context-validator),
         quick Q&A (use devox-assist).

workflows.name: devox-codebase-onboarding
workflows.description:
Use when: Starting work on an unfamiliar codebase, or onboarding a new agent to a project.
Input: None (analyzes current directory)
Does: Maps architecture → traces data flow → identifies patterns → generates tour document → saves to .devox/standards/
NOT for: Projects already well-understood; use devox-assist for specific questions.
Triggers: "onboard", "orient me", "understand this codebase", "codebase tour", "map the codebase", "learn the codebase"

workflows.name: devox-comprehensive-pr-review
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants a comprehensive code review of a pull request with automatic fixes.
Triggers: "review this PR", "review PR #123", "comprehensive review", "full PR review",
          "review and fix", "check this PR", "code review".
Does: Syncs PR with main (rebase if needed) -> runs 5 specialized review agents in parallel ->
      synthesizes findings -> auto-fixes CRITICAL/HIGH issues -> reports remaining issues.
NOT for: Quick questions about a PR, checking CI status, simple "what changed" queries.

This workflow produces artifacts in $ARTIFACTS_DIR/../reviews/pr-{number}/ and posts
a comprehensive review comment to the GitHub PR.

workflows.name: devox-continuous-learning
workflows.description:
Use when: At the end of a work session to extract learnings and save as instincts.
Input: None (analyzes current session context)
Does: Reviews session → extracts atomic learnings → assigns confidence scores → saves to ~/.devox/state/instincts.json (global, shared across all worktrees) → optionally promotes high-confidence instincts via approval gate → optionally deduplicates similar instincts via second approval gate
NOT for: Mid-session (run this when wrapping up work)
Triggers: "learn from this session", "extract learnings", "save instincts", "what did we learn", "continuous learning"

workflows.name: devox-cost-audit
workflows.description:
Use when: Auditing AI token usage, session cost, and harness bloat across workflow runs.
Input: Optional — number of runs to analyse (default: 10), or a specific run ID.
Does: Collects run stats → estimates cost per workflow/node → audits context overhead
      → checks harness for model waste → produces a prioritised savings report.
NOT for: Real-time session monitoring; use /context-budget mid-session for that.
Triggers: "cost audit", "token usage", "how much did that cost", "cost report",
          "token report", "audit costs", "am i over-spending", "harness audit",
          "cost analysis", "workflow cost"

workflows.name: devox-create-issue
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants to report a bug or problem as a GitHub issue with automated reproduction.
Triggers: "create issue", "file a bug", "report this bug", "open an issue for",
          "create github issue", "report issue", "log this bug".
Does: Classifies problem area (haiku) -> gathers context in parallel (templates, git state, duplicates) ->
      investigates relevant code -> reproduces the issue using area-specific tools (agent-browser, CLI, DB queries) ->
      gates on reproduction success -> creates issue with full evidence OR reports back if cannot reproduce.
NOT for: Feature requests, enhancements, or non-bug work. Only for bugs/problems.

Reproduction gating: If the issue cannot be reproduced, the workflow does NOT create an issue.
Instead, it reports what was tried and suggests next steps to the user.

workflows.name: devox-deep-research
workflows.description:
Use when: Need to research a technical topic deeply with multiple sources and synthesize findings.
Input: Research question or topic ($ARGUMENTS)
Does: Clarify scope → plan sources → search (adapts to available tools) → synthesize → deliver cited report
NOT for: Quick lookups; use devox-assist for simple questions.
Triggers: "research", "deep research", "investigate", "find out about", "learn about", "study"

workflows.name: devox-discover
workflows.description:
Use when: A user wants to explore what Devox can do, discover available workflows/commands/agents,

Input: Optional filter — "workflows", "commands", "agents", "hooks", "skills", or a use-case keyword
Does: Scans installed capabilities → reads project context → produces a personalized capability guide
      with examples relevant to the current codebase.
NOT for: Running capabilities (use the specific workflow/command). This is discovery only.
Triggers: "what can you do", "what workflows do I have", "show me capabilities",
          "discover devox", "what's available", "show me what's installed",
          "capabilities", "help me find a workflow", "what commands exist"

workflows.name: devox-enterprise-context-validator
workflows.description:
Use when: You have an idea, feature, or issue (inline text, file path, or Jira key) and need
          to resolve applicable enterprise rules BEFORE planning begins.
Triggers: "enterprise context", "resolve context", "get enterprise rules", "context resolver",
          "architecture context", "governance context", "design system context",
          "domain context", "domain model", "bounded context", "business capabilities",
          "enterprise domain", "compliance context", "regulatory context", "jira context".
Does: Ingests your input (inline / file / Jira), classifies it, then
      dynamically fetches and resolves enterprise rules across five domains in parallel:
  -> Input ingestion: auto-detects inline text, file path, or Jira issue key
  -> Enterprise standards fetched per domain from configured sources:
      Sources controlled by ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT_SOURCES (default: files,confluence,git)
      1. Physical files  (ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT_HOME/<configurable-subdir>/ or domain path override)
      2. Confluence      (domain-specific space or CONFLUENCE_STANDARDS_SPACE fallback)
      3. GitHub repo     (ENTERPRISE_STANDARDS_REPO)
      4. Codebase        (fallback: auto-discover from project files)
  -> Architecture principles, constraints, and integration patterns
  -> Design system tokens, components, UX patterns, and accessibility rules
  -> Governance policy (internal) + Regulatory compliance (GDPR, PCI-DSS, etc.)
  -> Enterprise domain model: bounded contexts, capabilities, ubiquitous language, events
  -> System landscape: service map, integration boundaries
  -> Token-optimised: targeted Confluence CQL + compact JSON classification output
  -> Risk Dashboard: traffic-light status on every rule, gap, and constraint
  -> Conflict resolution across all domains
  -> Unified Enterprise Context Package saved to artifacts
Outputs: enterprise-context.md — the binding rulebook for any downstream planning.
Reuse: This workflow produces the same Enterprise Context Package as Layer 2 of
       product-idea-to-enterprise-plan. Use it standalone when you already have a validated
       Mission Intent and want to resolve enterprise context independently.
       Called as a sub-workflow by product-idea-to-enterprise-plan (Layer 2).
Configuration (in ~/.devox/.env):

  Input ingestion (Jira):
  JIRA_BASE_URL   — Jira instance URL, e.g. https://myorg.atlassian.net
  JIRA_API_TOKEN  — Jira personal access token
  JIRA_EMAIL      — Jira account email (used with API token for Basic auth)

  Source selection (controls which sources are queried and in what order):
  ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT_SOURCES — Comma-separated ordered list. Default: files,confluence,git
                                Tokens: inline | files | confluence | git
                                (vectordb reserved for future use — accepted, no-op)
                                Examples:
                                  ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT_SOURCES=files
                                  ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT_SOURCES=files,confluence
                                  ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT_SOURCES=inline,files,confluence,git

  Enterprise-wide standards (organisation-level):
  ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT_HOME   — Path to shared enterprise standards directory.
                               Default subdirectory structure (all configurable below):
                                 architecture/  — principles.md, patterns/, ADRs
                                 design/        — guidelines.md, brand.md, accessibility.md
                                 governance/    — policy.md, compliance.md, security.md
                                 landscape/     — services.md, integrations.md, c4-context.md
                                 domain/        — bounded-contexts.md, capabilities.md,
                                                  glossary.md, entities.md, events.md

  Configurable subdirectory names within ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT_HOME:
  ENTERPRISE_ARCH_DIR       — default: architecture  (e.g. set to: arch, ea)
  ENTERPRISE_DESIGN_DIR     — default: design        (e.g. set to: ux, ux-standards)
  ENTERPRISE_GOVERNANCE_DIR — default: governance    (e.g. set to: risk, compliance)
  ENTERPRISE_LANDSCAPE_DIR  — default: landscape     (e.g. set to: c4, system-map)
  ENTERPRISE_DOMAIN_DIR     — default: domain        (e.g. set to: ddd, domain-model)

  Domain-specific full path overrides (bypass ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT_HOME):
  ARCHITECTURE_PRINCIPLES_PATH — Local dir/file with architecture principles
  DESIGN_GUIDELINES_PATH       — Local dir/file with design/brand guidelines
  GOVERNANCE_DOCS_PATH         — Local dir/file with governance/compliance docs
  SYSTEM_LANDSCAPE_PATH        — Local dir/file with system landscape/C4 docs
  DOMAIN_MODEL_PATH            — Local dir/file with domain model docs

  Confluence (per-domain spaces with shared fallback):
  CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL         — Confluence instance URL
  CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN        — Confluence personal access token
  CONFLUENCE_ARCH_SPACE       — Space key for architecture (falls back to CONFLUENCE_STANDARDS_SPACE)
  CONFLUENCE_DESIGN_SPACE     — Space key for design       (falls back to CONFLUENCE_STANDARDS_SPACE)
  CONFLUENCE_GOVERNANCE_SPACE — Space key for governance   (falls back to CONFLUENCE_STANDARDS_SPACE)
  CONFLUENCE_LANDSCAPE_SPACE  — Space key for landscape    (falls back to CONFLUENCE_STANDARDS_SPACE)
  CONFLUENCE_DOMAIN_SPACE     — Space key for domain model (falls back to CONFLUENCE_STANDARDS_SPACE)
  CONFLUENCE_STANDARDS_SPACE  — Shared fallback space key

  Legacy general standards (fallback):
  ENTERPRISE_STANDARDS_REPO — GitHub repo, e.g. acme-corp/arch-standards
  ENTERPRISE_STANDARDS_PATH — Local directory path

  Project-level (zero-config — create files in the target project repo):
  .devox/mission.md                  — Product scope contract (highest-authority override)
  .devox/standards/architecture/      — Architecture principles (all *.md in folder)
  .devox/standards/design/           — Design system guidelines (all *.md in folder)
  .devox/standards/governance/       — Governance & compliance rules (all *.md in folder)
  .devox/standards/domain/landscape.md — System landscape
  .devox/standards/domain/domain.md  — Domain model

  Context scope (to resolve only specific domains):
  ENTERPRISE_CONTEXT_DOMAINS — Comma-separated. Default: all
                                Values: architecture,design,governance,landscape,domain

NOT for: Idea validation (use product-idea-to-enterprise-plan for the full journey),
         feature planning without context (always resolve context first).

workflows.name: devox-feature-development
workflows.description:
Use when: Implementing a feature from an existing plan.
Input: Path to a plan file ($ARTIFACTS_DIR/plan.md) or GitHub issue containing a plan.
Does: Implements the plan with validation loops -> creates pull request.
NOT for: Creating plans (plans should be created separately), bug fixes, code reviews.
Triggers: "implement the plan", "feature development", "execute plan",
          "build from plan", "implement feature".

workflows.name: devox-fetch-design-guidelines
workflows.description:
Use when: You have an external design system or brand URL and want to extract
          its complete design guidelines into structured, reusable artifacts.
Triggers: "fetch design guidelines", "extract design system", "scrape design tokens",
          "get design guidelines from url", "design guidelines from website",
          "extract brand guidelines", "fetch component library", "design system docs",
          "download design guidelines", "design guidelines research".
Input: Any public design system or brand URL (e.g. https://material.io,
       https://ant.design, https://chakra-ui.com, https://www.ibm.com/design/language).
Does:
  Validates the URL, then runs 7 parallel extraction agents — each using web search
  to navigate the site and extract one category of design guidelines:
    1. Colors & Tokens     → 01-colors-tokens.md
    2. Typography          → 02-typography.md
    3. Spacing & Layout    → 03-spacing-layout.md
    4. Components          → components/index.md + per-component files
    5. Motion & Animation  → 04-motion-animation.md
    6. Accessibility       → 05-accessibility.md
    7. Brand & Voice       → 06-brand-voice.md
  All agents follow a strict output template (same structure every run).
  Finally, all sections are assembled into a single full-report.md.
Outputs (saved to $ARTIFACTS_DIR/design-guidelines/):
  00-index.md               — TOC + source URL + coverage summary
  01-colors-tokens.md       — Color palette, design tokens, themes
  02-typography.md          — Font families, type scale, weights
  03-spacing-layout.md      — Grid, spacing scale, breakpoints
  04-motion-animation.md    — Durations, easing, transition patterns
  05-accessibility.md       — WCAG level, focus patterns, contrast rules
  06-brand-voice.md         — Tone of voice, writing style, content patterns
  components/index.md       — Master list of all components found (with status)
  components/{name}.md      — Per-component: variants, states, props, do/don't, a11y
  full-report.md            — Single consolidated file (all sections merged)
NOT for: Generating new design systems (use devox-generate-design-overview),
         quick Q&A (use devox-assist).

workflows.name: devox-fix-github-issue
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants to FIX, RESOLVE, or IMPLEMENT a solution for a GitHub issue.
Triggers: "fix this issue", "implement issue #123", "resolve this bug", "fix it",
          "fix issue", "resolve issue", "fix #123".
NOT for: Comprehensive multi-agent reviews (use devox-issue-review-full),
         questions about issues, CI failures, PR reviews, general exploration.

DAG workflow that:
1. Classifies the issue (bug/feature/enhancement/etc)
2. Researches context (web research + codebase exploration via investigate/plan)
3. Routes to investigate (bugs) or plan (features) based on classification
4. Implements the fix/feature with validation
5. Creates a draft PR using the repo's PR template
6. Runs smart review (always code review + project conventions check, conditional additional agents)
7. Aggressively self-fixes all findings (tests, docs, error handling)
8. Simplifies changed code (implements fixes directly, not just reports)
9. Reports results back to the GitHub issue with follow-up suggestions

workflows.name: devox-full-lifecycle-interactive
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants to build a feature end-to-end using skills commands.
Input: Feature description ($ARGUMENTS)
Output: Merged PR with spec, plan, TDD implementation, review, and ship sign-off.

Every command node is a loop with interview-style interaction. 
Each phase runs iteratively: AI works, approval gate captures your
feedback, rejection re-runs the loop with your input until you approve and move on.

Full workflow:
1. Spec      — interview loop to write SPEC.md
2. [GATE]    — approve or reject with answers → re-runs spec loop
3. Plan      — interview loop to write tasks/plan.md + tasks/todo.md
4. [GATE]    — approve or reject with feedback → re-runs plan loop
5. Build     — loop: TDD one task at a time (unchanged)
6. Test      — loop: run tests, iterate on gaps
7. [GATE]    — approve or reject with targets → re-runs test loop
8. Review    — loop: 5-axis review, iterate on findings
9. [GATE]    — approve or reject to dig deeper → re-runs review loop
10. Simplify — loop: propose + apply simplifications
11. [GATE]   — approve or reject to adjust scope → re-runs simplify loop
12. Create PR — loop: draft and refine PR content
13. [GATE]   — approve or reject to revise → re-runs create-pr loop
14. Ship     — loop: parallel fan-out GO/NO-GO
15. [GATE]   — approve to merge or reject to fix blockers → re-runs ship loop

NOT for: Quick fixes (use devox-fix-issue). Existing plans (use devox-plan-to-pr).
Triggers: "full lifecycle", "build feature interactively", "interactive feature development",
          "spec plan build review ship".

workflows.name: devox-generate-design-overview
workflows.description:
Use when: You have a validated idea or feature (Mission Intent approved) and need
          high-level visual design artifacts BEFORE writing detailed specs.
Triggers: "design overview", "high level design", "hld", "sketch the system",
          "architecture overview", "ux flow diagram", "system diagram",
          "design sketch", "architecture sketch", "draw the system",
          "visualise the architecture", "design diagrams", "system overview",
          "c4 diagram", "c4 model", "c4 context", "c4 container", "system context diagram".
Does:
  Reads the Mission Intent Snapshot and Enterprise Context Package from artifacts
  (or $ARGUMENTS in standalone mode) and produces SIX diagrams:
  1. UX Flow Diagram — screens, user transitions, decision branches, error paths (Mermaid flowchart TD)
  2. Architecture Context Diagram — actors, boundary, services, external systems (Mermaid graph TB)
  3. Sequence Diagram — primary happy-path interactions across all layers (Mermaid sequenceDiagram)
  4. C4 System Context Diagram — external actors + system boundary (Mermaid C4Context)
  5. C4 Container Diagram — internal containers, services, databases (Mermaid C4Container)
  6. ER Diagram — data entities, relationships, cardinality, audit columns (Mermaid erDiagram)
  Diagrams 1–3 are standard Mermaid. Diagrams 4–5 follow the C4 model (Simon Brown) using
  Mermaid's C4Context and C4Container grammar. All five diagrams are consistent in actors/names.
  Enterprise context rules (from Layer 2) are applied when available.
  Standalone mode includes an approval gate for human review.
Outputs (saved to $ARTIFACTS_DIR):
  hld/ux-flow.md              — Mermaid flowchart TD: UX screens + transitions
  hld/architecture-context.md — Mermaid graph TB: system actors + service boundaries
  hld/sequence-diagram.md     — Mermaid sequenceDiagram: primary happy-path
  hld/c4-system-context.md    — Mermaid C4Context: actors + system boundary (C4 Level 1)
  hld/c4-container.md         — Mermaid C4Container: containers + databases (C4 Level 2)
  hld/er-diagram.md           — Mermaid erDiagram: data entities + relationships (ER Model)
Works as:
  Standalone: run after concept-validation and devox-enterprise-context-validator have saved artifacts.
  Sub-workflow: called by product-idea-to-enterprise-plan after Gates 1 and 2.
NOT for: Detailed UX specifications (use devox-build-ready-plan Section 6),
         architecture design decisions (ADRs are in devox-build-ready-plan Section 7),
         quick Q&A (use devox-assist).

workflows.name: devox-generic-request-validation
workflows.description:
Use when: You have a raw idea, feature request, enhancement, or bug and want to:
          - Validate it against project scope (alignment check)
          - Classify it (idea | feature | enhancement | bug)
          - Run multi-persona validation for ideas and features
          - Get a GO / VALIDATE FURTHER / NO-GO decision with a Mission Intent Snapshot
Triggers: "validate concept", "validate idea", "is this worth building",
          "concept validation", "idea validation", "assess this feature",
          "evaluate this idea", "go no-go check", "idea check", "validate requirement",
          "validate feature", "check my idea", "idea assessment", "concept check".
Does:
  Standalone mode (run directly with $ARGUMENTS):
    [Delegates to request-classifier sub-workflow: Gate 0, classification, alignment check,
     and alignment gate on MAJOR_DEVIATION — all handled inside request-classifier]
    Full multi-persona validation for idea/feature (full path):
      Product Strategist intake → parallel [Market | UX | Finance | Feasibility]
      → CPO consolidation → GO / VALIDATE FURTHER / NO-GO
    [Gate 1: Human reviews and edits the Mission Intent Snapshot]
    Enhancement path: produces planning brief
    Bug path: classification + alignment summary with guidance
  Sub-workflow mode (called by product-idea-to-enterprise-plan):
    Reads idea text and classification from artifacts/request/ (written by request-classifier)
    Skips request-classifier entirely (context.json already present)
    Runs L1 multi-persona validation for full path only
    Saves artifacts for the orchestrator's Gate 1 to display
    Gate 1 fires in this mode too — human-edited mission intent is written to disk for downstream
Outputs (saved to $ARTIFACTS_DIR):
  request-generic-validation/mission-intent.md    — GO/NO-GO + Mission Intent Snapshot (full path)
  request-generic-validation/enhancement-brief.md — Planning brief (enhancement path, standalone)
  request-generic-validation/classification.json  — Input type + routing path (always)
NOT for: Detailed build planning (use devox-build-ready-plan), quick Q&A (use devox-assist),
         enterprise context only (use devox-enterprise-context-validator),
         full enterprise planning journey (use product-idea-to-enterprise-plan).

workflows.name: devox-hookify
workflows.description:
Use when: Setting up Claude/Copilot hooks for a project — security scanning, session-start context, instinct extraction.
Input: Which hooks to enable ($ARGUMENTS: "all", "security", "learning", "session", "audit", or space-separated names)
Does: Creates .claude/hooks/ directory → writes hook scripts → configures hooks in settings.json → tests each hook
NOT for: Codex or Pi (use script: workflow nodes instead)
Triggers: "hookify", "set up hooks", "add hooks", "configure hooks", "hook my project", "add session hooks"

workflows.name: devox-idea-to-pr
workflows.description:
Use when: You have a feature idea or description and want end-to-end development.
Input: Feature description in natural language, or path to a PRD file
Output: PR ready for merge with comprehensive review completed

Full workflow:
1. Create comprehensive implementation plan with codebase analysis
2. Setup branch and extract scope limits
3. Verify plan research is still valid
4. Implement all tasks with type-checking
5. Run full validation suite
6. Create PR with template, mark ready
7. Comprehensive code review (5 parallel agents with scope limit awareness)
8. Synthesize and fix review findings
9. Final summary with decision matrix -> GitHub comment + follow-up recommendations

NOT for: Executing existing plans (use devox-plan-to-pr), quick fixes, standalone reviews.
Triggers: "idea to pr", "turn idea into pr", "build feature from scratch",
          "implement this idea", "develop and ship".

workflows.name: devox-implement
workflows.description:
Use when: Executing an implementation plan end-to-end with mandatory verification.
Input: Path to a plan file or GitHub issue URL/number containing the plan.
Does: Runs devox-implement command → mandatory devox-verification-loop sub-workflow
      → optional continuous-learning capture at session end.
NOT for: Creating plans (use devox-plan), pure bug fixes, code reviews.
Triggers: "implement the plan", "execute plan", "build from plan", "implement feature",
          "implement this", "run the implementation".

workflows.name: devox-init-project
workflows.description:
Use when: User has just added a new project and wants to bootstrap governance files.
Triggers: "initialize project", "init project", "bootstrap governance", "setup project rules",
          "generate governance files", "create AGENTS.md", "create CLAUDE.md".
Does: Checks gh auth -> scans tech stack -> writes 4 governance files ->
      runs graphify-init as a sub-workflow (same worktree) to build the knowledge graph ->
      commits everything together (governance + graphify-out/) -> validates ->
      creates and merges a single PR with all initialisation artifacts.
NOT for: Feature development, bug fixes, general project analysis (use devox-architect).

DAG nodes:
- check-auth       (bash)      → 'ok' | 'gh-missing' | 'not-authenticated'
- auth-required    (approval)  → pause if not authenticated
- scan-project     (bash)      → detect tech stack and structure
- check-graph      (bash)      → 'exists' | 'missing' (runs in parallel with scan-project)
- load-graph-early (bash)      → fast --update if graph exists; skip if missing
- analyze-architecture (prompt) → read source files; understand real architecture
- write-mission    (prompt)    → writes MISSION.md to $ARTIFACTS_DIR
- write-guardrails (prompt)    → writes GUARDRAILS.md to $ARTIFACTS_DIR
- write-agents     (prompt)    → writes AGENTS.md to $ARTIFACTS_DIR
- write-claude-md  (prompt)    → writes CLAUDE.md to $ARTIFACTS_DIR
- deploy-files     (bash)      → verifies AI wrote files, copies to CWD
- review-docs      (approval)  → artifact links for user to open, edit, then approve
- init-graphify    (workflow)  → graphify-init sub-workflow in same worktree; builds graph + wires platform skill
- commit-files     (bash)      → git add governance files + graphify output + commit
- validate-files   (bash)      → verify all 4 files exist and are non-empty
- create-pr        (bash)      → push branch + gh pr create → base branch
- merge-pr         (bash)      → gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch (isolation-safe)

Governance files:
- MISSION.md       — what the project is; hard invariants; out-of-scope; allowed evolutions
- GUARDRAILS.md — how the AI factory operates; triage/impl/validation/merge rules
- AGENTS.md        — redirect to CLAUDE.md (all agents share same instructions)
- CLAUDE.md        — comprehensive agent guide (all providers); build/test/lint; architecture; conventions

workflows.name: devox-interactive-prd
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants to create a PRD through guided conversation.
Triggers: "create a prd", "new prd", "interactive prd", "plan a feature",
          "product requirements", "write a prd".
NOT for: Autonomous PRD generation without human input (use devox-ralph-generate).

Interactive workflow that guides the user through problem-first PRD creation:
1. Understand the idea → ask foundation questions → wait for answers
2. Research market & codebase → ask deep dive questions → wait for answers
3. Assess technical feasibility → ask scope questions → wait for answers
4. Generate PRD → validate technical claims against codebase → output

workflows.name: devox-issue-review-full
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants a FULL, COMPREHENSIVE fix + review pipeline for a GitHub issue.
Triggers: "full review", "comprehensive fix", "fix with full review", "deep review", "issue review full".
NOT for: Simple issue fixes (use devox-fix-github-issue instead),
         questions about issues, CI failures, PR reviews, general exploration.

Full workflow:
1. Investigate issue -> root cause analysis, implementation plan
2. Implement fix -> code changes, tests, PR creation
3. Comprehensive review -> 5 parallel agents with scope awareness
4. Fix review issues -> address CRITICAL/HIGH findings
5. Final summary -> decision matrix, follow-up recommendations

workflows.name: devox-kanban-to-pr
workflows.description:
Use when: Implementation of a Kanban board idea has been triggered via the Devox Web UI.
Triggered by: POST /api/ideas/:id/trigger-implementation (not by chat directly).

DAG workflow that:
1. Fetches all board tasks (features + issues) for the idea from the Devox API
2. Creates GitHub issues for all tasks (idempotent — skips already-created issues)
   Labels: devox + type:{feature|bug|enhancement} + req:{request-slug} for filtering
   Title: [RequestName] Task title  |  Body: Request → User Story → Task hierarchy
3. Builds a context snapshot of the codebase to understand patterns before implementing
4. Implements each task sequentially in a loop — one commit per task, updating board status per step
5. Validates: type-check + lint + tests
6. Creates a single draft PR closing all GitHub issues
7. Runs comprehensive parallel code review
8. Auto-fixes all critical/high findings
9. Simplifies changed code
10. Posts PR link back to each GitHub issue and updates board idea status

Isolation: Runs inside a single worktree (devox/task-{idea-slug}) created by the orchestrator
before the workflow starts. All tasks commit to this one branch.
Triggers: "internal workflow".

workflows.name: devox-piv-loop
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants guided Plan-Implement-Validate development with human-in-the-loop.
Triggers: "piv", "piv loop", "plan implement validate", "guided development",
          "structured development", "build a feature", "develop with review".
NOT for: Autonomous implementation without planning (use devox-feature-development).
NOT for: PRD creation (use devox-interactive-prd).
NOT for: Ralph story-based implementation (use devox-ralph-dag).

Interactive PIV loop workflow — the foundational AI coding methodology:
1. EXPLORE: Iterative conversation with human to understand the problem (arbitrary rounds)
2. PLAN: Create structured plan -> iterative review & revision (arbitrary rounds)
3. IMPLEMENT: Autonomous task-by-task implementation from plan (Ralph loop)
4. VALIDATE: Automated code review -> iterative human feedback & fixes (arbitrary rounds)

The PIV loop comes AFTER a PRD exists. Each PIV loop focuses on ONE granular feature or bug fix.
Input: A description of what to build, a path to an existing plan, or a GitHub issue number.

workflows.name: devox-plan-to-backlog
workflows.description:
Use when: A plan has been approved for an idea or feature and you need to break it into a
          structured backlog ready for development. Triggered by the "Plan Backlog" button in
          the Kanban UI after idea.status = approved.
Triggers: "plan backlog", "create backlog", "break down plan", "user stories", "create tasks",
          "backlog items", "feature list", "task list", "plan to backlog".
Does: Reads the approved plan artifact from $ARTIFACTS_DIR and generates structured user stories
  covering all types (Feature, Enhancement, Bug, Technical, Spike) with acceptance criteria,
  priority, and estimate. Presents a human-in-the-loop approval gate with an editable editor —
  reviewers can update titles, descriptions, acceptance criteria, or priority before approving.
  Rejected drafts are regenerated with reviewer feedback (up to 2 attempts).
  On approval, three things happen in parallel:
    1. Stories saved to $ARTIFACTS_DIR/stories/ (pure bash — no AI overhead)
    2. Feature / Issue records created in the Devox ideas DB (bash + bun script)
    3. Issues pushed to Jira if Atlassian MCP is configured (save-to-jira command)
  DB and Jira steps are non-blocking — workflow completes even if either is unavailable.
  Run 'create-tasks' afterwards to generate granular implementation tasks per story.
Outputs (saved to $ARTIFACTS_DIR):
  stories/{plan-name}-stories.md  — final approved stories with full structure
NOT for: Raw idea → plan generation (use product-idea-to-enterprise-plan).
         Direct code implementation.

workflows.name: devox-plan-to-pr
workflows.description:
Use when: You have an existing implementation plan and want to execute it end-to-end.
Input: Path to a plan file ($ARTIFACTS_DIR/plan.md or .agents/plans/*.md)
Output: PR ready for merge with comprehensive review completed

Full workflow:
1. Read plan, setup branch, extract scope limits
2. Verify plan research is still valid
3. Implement all tasks with type-checking
4. Run full validation suite
5. Create PR with template, mark ready
6. Comprehensive code review (5 parallel agents with scope limit awareness)
7. Synthesize and fix review findings
8. Final summary with decision matrix -> GitHub comment + follow-up recommendations

NOT for: Creating plans from scratch (use devox-idea-to-pr), quick fixes, standalone reviews.
Triggers: "plan to pr", "execute this plan", "implement plan and create pr", "ship this plan".

workflows.name: devox-plannotator-piv
workflows.description:
Use when: You want a plan-gated feature build where the plan is reviewed via
plannotator's HTTP approval UI instead of chat back-and-forth.
Triggers: "plannotator piv", "plan with plannotator", "build with plannotator gate".
NOT for: Fully-chat-driven PIV (use devox-piv-loop), quick fixes, PR reviews.

Four phases:
1. CLARIFY: Claude asks 2-3 targeted questions via Devox HITL, converges on intent.
2. PLAN: Pi session writes PLAN.md and submits it to plannotator. The reviewer
   receives a 127.0.0.1:19432 URL and approves (or denies with feedback — Pi
   iterates on the plan inside its session until approved).
3. IMPLEMENT: Claude reads the approved PLAN.md and executes task-by-task
   with per-task validation + commits.
4. VALIDATE: Final full validation + summary.

workflows.name: devox-ralph-dag
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants to run a Ralph implementation loop.
Triggers: "ralph", "run ralph", "ralph dag", "run ralph dag".

DAG workflow that:
1. Detects input: existing prd.json, existing prd.md (needs stories), or raw idea
2. Generates prd.md + prd.json if needed (explores codebase, breaks into stories)
3. Validates PRD files, reads project context, installs dependencies
4. Runs Ralph loop (fresh context per iteration) implementing one story per iteration
5. Creates PR and reports completion

Accepts: An idea description, a path to an existing prd.md, or a directory with prd.md + prd.json

workflows.name: devox-refactor-safely
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants to refactor code safely with continuous validation and behavior preservation.
Triggers: "refactor", "refactor safely", "split this file", "extract module", "break up",
          "decompose", "safe refactor", "split file", "extract into modules".
Does: Scans refactoring scope -> analyzes impact (read-only) -> plans ordered task list ->
      executes with type-check hooks after every edit -> validates full suite ->
      verifies behavior preservation (read-only) -> creates PR with before/after comparison.
NOT for: Bug fixes (use devox-fix-github-issue), feature development (use devox-feature-development),
         general architecture sweeps (use devox-architect), PR reviews.

Key safety features:
- Analysis and verification nodes are read-only (denied_tools: [Write, Edit, Bash])
- PreToolUse hooks check if each edit is in the plan
- PostToolUse hooks force type-check after every file change
- Behavior verification confirms no logic changes after refactoring

workflows.name: devox-remotion-generate
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants to generate or modify a Remotion video composition using AI.
Triggers: "create a video", "generate video", "remotion", "make an animation",
          "video about", "animate".
Does: AI writes Remotion React code -> renders preview stills -> renders full video ->
      summarizes the output.
Requires: A Remotion project in the working directory (src/index.ts, src/Root.tsx).
Optional: Install the remotion-best-practices skill for higher quality output:
          npx skills add remotion-dev/skills

workflows.name: devox-request-classifier
workflows.description:
Use when: Called as a sub-workflow to perform the standard request classification phase.
          Gate 0 (human request review) lives in the parent workflow.
          The alignment gate (MAJOR_DEVIATION override) is handled here, inside request-classifier,
          so the sub-workflow is fully self-contained and easy to re-run or modify.
Used by:  concept-validation (standalone mode) and product-idea-to-enterprise-plan.
Does:
  Receives the pre-reviewed canonical request text via $DEVOX_ARGUMENTS (passed by parent).
  Classifies the input (idea | feature | enhancement | bug) and derives routing_path
    (full | lite | bug) in parallel with the project alignment scan.
  Runs AI project alignment check against mission.md / guardrails.md / agents.md / CLAUDE.md.
  Fires alignment-gate ONLY on MAJOR_DEVIATION — human must approve override or reject.
  Writes all outputs to $ARTIFACTS_DIR/request/ for downstream workflows to consume.
Outputs (saved to $ARTIFACTS_DIR/request/):
  context.json      — orchestration manifest { contract_version, routing_path, input_type,
                      title, summary, planning_brief_source, alignment_status }
  request.md        — canonical request text (from $DEVOX_ARGUMENTS)
  alignment.json    — full alignment check result { alignment_status, deviation_summary,
                      specific_violations, guidance, minor_flags }
  alignment-scan.md — raw project definition files (used by bug-triage / enhancement-brief)
NOT for: Direct use by end users — always called as a sub-workflow.
Triggers: "internal workflow".

workflows.name: devox-resolve-conflicts
workflows.description:
Use when: PR has merge conflicts that need resolution.
Triggers: "resolve conflicts", "fix merge conflicts", "rebase this PR", "resolve this",
          "fix conflicts", "merge conflicts", "rebase and fix".
Does: Fetches latest base branch -> analyzes conflicts -> auto-resolves simple conflicts ->
      presents options for complex conflicts -> commits and pushes resolution.
NOT for: PRs without conflicts, general rebasing without conflicts, squashing commits.

This workflow helps resolve merge conflicts by analyzing the conflicting changes,
automatically resolving where intent is clear, and presenting options for complex conflicts.

workflows.name: devox-security-audit
workflows.description:

Input: Optional scope (file path, "recent" for last 5 commits, or "full" for entire codebase)
Does: Discovers attack surface → scans for secrets → audits deps → reviews auth/injection → synthesizes report → optionally creates issues

Triggers: "security audit", "security review", "audit security", "check for vulnerabilities", "security scan"

workflows.name: devox-smart-pr-review
workflows.description:

Triggers: "smart review", "review this PR", "review PR #123", "efficient review",

Does: Gathers PR scope -> classifies complexity -> routes to only relevant review agents ->

NOT for: When you explicitly want ALL review agents (use devox-comprehensive-pr-review instead).

Unlike the comprehensive review, this workflow classifies the PR first and only runs
the review agents that are relevant. A 3-line typo fix skips test-coverage and docs-impact.

workflows.name: devox-tdd

workflows.name: devox-test-loop-dag

workflows.name: devox-token-compare

workflows.name: devox-validate-pr
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants a thorough PR validation that tests both main (bug present) and feature branch (bug fixed).
Triggers: "validate PR", "validate pr #123", "test this PR", "verify PR", "full PR validation",
          "validate pull request", "test PR end-to-end".
Does: Fetches PR info -> finds free ports -> parallel code review (main vs feature) ->
      E2E test on main (reproduce bug) -> E2E test on feature (verify fix) -> final verdict report.
NOT for: Quick code-only reviews (use devox-smart-pr-review), fixing issues, general exploration.

This workflow is designed for running in parallel — each instance finds its own free ports
to avoid conflicts. Produces artifacts in $ARTIFACTS_DIR/ and posts a validation report.

workflows.description:
Use when: Verifying code quality after any implementation. Can be run standalone or called as a sub-workflow.

NOT for: During active development (run this after you think you're done)

workflows.name: generate-wireframes
workflows.description:
Use when: You have run product-idea-to-enterprise-plan and want to generate an
          interactive wireframe prototype from the UX specification it produced.
          Can also run standalone with a manual description via $ARGUMENTS.

Triggers: "generate wireframes", "create wireframes", "wireframe prototype",
          "build prototype", "create prototype", "ui prototype", "wireframe screens".

Does:
  Reads ux-specification.md + enterprise design context + UX flow diagram from
  artifacts (sub-workflow mode) OR from $ARGUMENTS (standalone mode).
  Selects a wireframe engine via WIREFRAME_ENGINE env var (default: react-tailwind).
  Generates the prototype, then presents a simple approve / reject gate.
  No text input required at the gate — pure approve or reject.

Engines (set via WIREFRAME_ENGINE in ~/.devox/.env):
  react-tailwind  (default) — self-contained index.html, no build step, open directly
                              in any browser. Uses React 18 + Tailwind CSS via CDN.
  excalidraw                — .excalidraw JSON file. Open at excalidraw.com or
                              self-hosted instance. Hand-drawn wireframe style.

Adding a new engine later:
  1. Add a new node with: when: "$detect-engine.output == 'your-engine'"
  2. Add your engine name to the supported list in detect-engine script.
  3. No other nodes need changing — preview-summary and wireframe-review are universal.

Outputs (saved to $ARTIFACTS_DIR/wireframes/<engine>/):
  react-tailwind: index.html + README.md
  excalidraw:     screens.excalidraw + README.md

How to test (standalone — no prior workflow run needed):
  bun run cli workflow run generate-wireframes "A login screen, a dashboard, and a settings page"

How to use after product-idea-to-enterprise-plan:
  Run product-idea-to-enterprise-plan first, note its run ID.
  Then run this workflow — it auto-reads artifacts from the same ARTIFACTS_DIR.

How to switch engine:
  WIREFRAME_ENGINE=excalidraw bun run cli workflow run generate-wireframes

NOT for: Full enterprise planning (use product-idea-to-enterprise-plan),
         code implementation (use devox-plan-to-pr).

workflows.name: graphify-init
workflows.description:
Use when: You want to index a repository with graphify for graph-guided AI navigation.
Does: Six steps —
      (1) installs graphify globally via brew/uv/pip (skipped if already installed),
      (2) detects the active coding agent platform,
      (3) installs the graphify skill for the detected platform (skipped if already installed),
          uses exact "Pick your platform" commands from the graphify README,
      (4) builds or refreshes the knowledge graph — `graphify .` on first run,
          `graphify . --update` on subsequent runs (re-extracts only changed files, fast),
      (5) wires the agent to always use the graph — `graphify <platform> install` from the
          project directory so the agent reads GRAPH_REPORT.md before answering codebase questions,
      (6) sets up the repo: updates .gitignore and installs a git post-commit hook
          so the graph auto-rebuilds after every commit (AST only, no API cost).
Input: Optional $ARGUMENTS = target path (default: current directory ".")
Output: graphify-out/ committed to the repo. Run once per project, then /workflow graphify-update for updates.
NOT for: Answering questions (use graphify-assist), making code changes.
Triggers: "init graphify", "graphify init", "index repository",
          "setup graphify", "build knowledge graph".

workflows.name: piv-system-evolution
workflows.description:
Use when: User wants guided Plan-Implement-Validate development that also evolves the
codebase's AI Layer.
Triggers: "piv system evolution", "piv loop and evolve", "fix and improve the ai layer",
          "guided development with system evolution".
NOT for: Autonomous implementation with no human review (use devox-feature-development).
NOT for: PRD creation (use devox-interactive-prd).

The PIV loop (Plan -> Implement -> Validate) on one feature or bug, with a closing
system-evolution phase: the run's friction is turned into concrete AI-Layer improvements
(CLAUDE.md, command prompts, references) that a human curates before they are committed.

Four human-in-the-loop gates: after priming, after planning, after implementation,
and at the end. The autonomous phases are adapted from the agentic-coding-course AI Layer.
Input: a GitHub issue number, a feature description, or a path to a plan file.
Ends in a draft PR on an isolated worktree branch.

workflows.name: product-idea-to-enterprise-plan
workflows.description:
Use when: User has a raw idea, feature request, enhancement, or bug report and wants a full
          enterprise-grade build-ready plan produced with human checkpoints.
Triggers: "idea to plan", "validate idea", "enterprise plan", "product idea", "feature planning",
          "idea validation", "start fresh idea", "enterprise feature", "idea to enterprise".
Does: Full enterprise product development journey in four layers with five human checkpoints:
  [Gate 0: Human reviews submitted idea/requirement and can edit it before any processing.]
  [Alignment Check: AI validates request against mission.md, guardrails.md, agents.md, claude.md.
   Alignment gate (MAJOR_DEVIATION override) fires inside the request-classifier sub-workflow.]
  Layer 1: Concept validation (sub-workflow: devox-generic-request-validation)
    → Multi-persona idea validation (Product Strategist → Market/UX/Finance/Feasibility → CPO → Mission Intent)
  [Gate 1: Human reviews Mission Intent Snapshot. Can approve, modify, or reject to regenerate.]
  Layer 2: Enterprise context resolution (sub-workflow: devox-enterprise-context-validator)
    → Fetches enterprise standards (Confluence → GitHub repo → local files → codebase fallback)
    → Classifies feature + retrieves Architecture/Design-System/Governance context in parallel
    → Resolves cross-domain conflicts → Enterprise Context Package
  [Gate 2: Human reviews enterprise rulebook. Can add overrides, resolve conflicts, or stop.]
  HLD Phase: High-level design diagrams (sub-workflow: devox-generate-design-overview)
    → UX Flow Diagram (Mermaid flowchart TD: screens + transitions + decisions)
    → Architecture Context Diagram (Mermaid graph TB: actors + services + boundaries)
    → Sequence Diagram (Mermaid sequenceDiagram: primary happy-path)
    → C4 System Context Diagram (Mermaid C4Context: actors + system boundary)
    → C4 Container Diagram (Mermaid C4Container: containers + databases)
    → ER Diagram (Mermaid erDiagram: data entities + relationships + cardinality)
  [Gate HLD: Human reviews all six diagrams. Can approve or reject to regenerate.]
  Layer 3: Feature planning (sub-workflow: devox-build-ready-plan)
    → Multi-persona planning enforcing enterprise rules + grounded in HLD diagrams
    → Features List → cross-domain conflict resolution → build-ready plan
  Bug path: Inline triage + fix plan (no sub-workflows, no L1/L2/HLD/L3).
  Enhancement path: Inline planning brief → directly to devox-build-ready-plan sub-workflow.
Outputs (saved to $ARTIFACTS_DIR):
  request/context.json               — orchestration manifest (routing path, planning brief source)
  request-generic-validation/mission-intent.md         — GO/VALIDATE FURTHER/NO-GO + Mission Intent Snapshot
  enterprise-request-validator/enterprise-context.md — binding architecture, design system, and governance rules
  hld/ux-flow.md                   — Mermaid UX flow diagram (screens + transitions)
  hld/architecture-context.md      — Mermaid architecture context diagram (actors + services)
  hld/sequence-diagram.md          — Mermaid sequence diagram (primary happy-path)
  hld/c4-system-context.md         — Mermaid C4Context: actors + system boundary (C4 Level 1)
  hld/c4-container.md              — Mermaid C4Container: containers + databases (C4 Level 2)
  hld/er-diagram.md                — Mermaid erDiagram: data entities + relationships (ER Model)
  build-ready-plan/build-plan.md             — complete PRD, features list, architecture spec, UX spec, governance
  build-ready-plan/executive-summary.md      — concise summary for stakeholders
  bug/triage.md + bug/fix-plan.md  — (bug path only)
Sub-workflows:
  - request-classifier           (Phase 0 — request classification: Gate 0, classification, alignment)
  - devox-generic-request-validation  (Layer 1 — idea/feature validation, standalone or sub-workflow)
  - devox-enterprise-context-validator (Layer 2 — enterprise rules, standalone or sub-workflow)
  - devox-generate-design-overview (HLD phase — Mermaid diagrams, standalone or sub-workflow)
  - devox-build-ready-plan       (Layer 3 — detailed specs, standalone or sub-workflow)
External standards configuration (in ~/.devox/.env):
  CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL + CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN + CONFLUENCE_STANDARDS_SPACE (Confluence)
  ENTERPRISE_STANDARDS_REPO (GitHub repo)
  ENTERPRISE_STANDARDS_PATH (local filesystem)
Isolation: Runs in a fresh git worktree by default. Use --no-worktree to skip isolation.
NOT for: Pure code implementation (use devox-plan-to-pr), quick Q&A (use devox-assist),
         standalone enterprise context only (use devox-enterprise-context-validator),
         standalone HLD diagrams only (use devox-generate-design-overview).

workflows.name: spec-decompose
workflows.description:
Use when: You have an approved tech-spec and need individual executable task files.
Input: Path to an approved tech-spec.md file.
Does: Reads the tech spec, assigns execution waves, generates one task file per
implementation task, then validates each with the task-validator agent.
Output: .agents/specs/{feature}/tasks/{wave}-{NNN}-{title}.md files
NOT for: Creating GitHub issues (use devox-plan-to-backlog),
         Jira stories (use create-stories),
         executing the tasks (use execute command or devox-feature-development).
Triggers: "decompose tech spec", "spec-decompose", "create task files from spec",
          "break down tech spec", "task decomposition".

workflows.name: spec-driven-feature
workflows.description:
Use when: You want the full spec-first pipeline from feature idea to implementation.
Input: Feature name or description.
Does: Runs the complete spec-driven pipeline:
  1. Structured user interview → user-spec.md (with approval gate)
  2. Codebase research + parallel validation → tech-spec.md (with approval gate)
  3. Task decomposition → task files with TDD anchors
  4. Delegates to devox-feature-development workflow for implementation
NOT for: Features with an existing approved spec (run spec-tech directly),
         quick implementation without a spec (use devox-feature-development),
         features managed via GitHub issues (use devox-feature-e2e-delivery).
Triggers: "spec driven feature", "full spec pipeline", "spec first then implement",
          "spec to code", "spec driven development".

workflows.name: spec-tech
workflows.description:
Use when: You have an approved user-spec and need a technical specification.
Input: Path to an approved user-spec.md file.
Does: Runs 4 parallel codebase research threads, writes a tech spec with TDD anchors,
then validates with 5 parallel validators (skeptic, completeness, security,
test-strategy, structure).
NOT for: Project-level planning (use devox-feature-requirements-planning),
         features without an approved user-spec,
         quick implementation without a spec (use devox-feature-development directly).
Triggers: "write tech spec", "technical specification", "spec-tech",
          "create tech spec from", "technical spec for".

workflows.name: spec-user
workflows.description:
Use when: Starting a new feature and need a requirements spec before writing any code.
Input: Feature name or description.
Does: Runs a structured 3-cycle interview with the user, validates completeness and
reality of the spec, and produces an approved user-spec.md.
NOT for: Quick PRDs without validation (use devox-interactive-prd),
         product-level planning (use product-idea-to-enterprise-plan),
         features that already have an approved spec.
Triggers: "write user spec", "create requirements spec", "spec-user",
          "interview me about this feature", "write a spec for".
